summary.text: A 38-year-old male had bilateral mandibular CHF and a symphyseal fracture resulting from interpersonal violence. He presented with limited jaw opening, bilateral preauricular swelling, malocclusion and frontal open bite. High-resolution CT showed bilateral AO type-p fractures with lost vertical apposition, no fragmentation on the right and minor fragmentation on the left.

Interactive virtual surgical planning led to a patient-specific device intended for removal at the end of the operation. The symphyseal fracture was fixed with two miniplates and the right CHF was exposed through a preauricular approach. The PSD obstructed the fracture line, so a grid plate was used for prefixation, the PSD was mounted for reinforcement and two small-fragment screws were inserted. Left-side ORIF was deferred.
Postoperative Panorex confirmed adequate reduction and fixation. Functional treatment with elastics was performed for three weeks.

summary.text: A 13-year-old boy had a right mandibular CHF caused by a fall, with limited jaw opening and contralateral open bite. CT showed an AO type-p CHF with no fragmentation but lost vertical apposition; the medial fragment had an atypical rectangular shape and was displaced antero-medially and angulated caudally.

Virtual planning mirrored the contralateral condylar head, which ignored the medial fragment shape and eventually led to suboptimal fit of a P-shaped PSD. The PSD bridged the fracture, the flat fragment allowed LSFPSO with one screw only, and the PSD was left in situ as stand-by. Postoperative CT confirmed proper reduction and fixation, and elastics were used for 10 days.

At seven months postoperatively bony consolidation was observed, though screw and plate loosening necessitated hardware removal, and CT at 7 months showed loosening of the PSD fixation screws. Preinjury occlusion was stable and jaw opening unrestricted.

summary.text: A 59-year-old woman had a right CHF that was initially treated non-surgically. She presented with malocclusion and right temporomandibular joint pain 16 months post injury. Imaging revealed deformation of the right condylar head with vertical ramus height loss due to medial fragment displacement.

Virtual planning led to a crescent-shaped osteotomy with PSD-assisted fixation, and a large rigid P-shaped PSD was designed because of the resulting osteotomy gap. A piezosurgery osteotomy was performed, the medial segment was repositioned and the PSD applied uneventfully. Poor bone quality limited prefixation, an irregular gap remained, and the second LSFPSO screw was inserted free hand. X-rays confirmed adequate reduction.

Six months postoperatively the patient developed right-sided preauricular pain and restricted jaw opening, and CT-Imaging revealed contact of the PSD with the glenoid fossa. Hardware removal alleviated symptoms, and further follow-up was unremarkable.

evidence.quote: A three-component multi-purpose PSD was designed. In line with previous cases, one PSD component of the PSD was designated to reduction and prefixation. To address the difficulties in stabilizing the dislocated largest medial fragment alongside smaller pieces, the upper PSD portion was equipped with four finger-like extensions along the entire posterior surface of the condylar head. summary.text: A 62-year-old man had a left mandibular multi-fragmented CHF following a bike accident, with severe occlusal disturbances and ipsilateral open bite. CT showed a left AO type-p CHF with multi-fragmentation (three major fragments), loss of vertical apposition and anteromedial displacement.

A three-component multi-purpose PSD tool set was designed, with a reduction/prefixation component, a navigation/washer component, drill guides and a T-shaped implant. At surgery the fragments were reassembled and reduced, but repeated attempts to position the reduction/prefixation PSD failed. Salvage used a conventional grid plate, washer-guided entry points and two LSFPSO screws, after which the grid plate was removed.
A postoperative panoramic X-ray confirmed anatomical reduction of the fracture. At clinical follow-up the patient was asymptomatic with unimpaired function.
